verdict.rationale: Databricks SQL documents running 'directly on your data lake' with Delta Lake 'without moving your data', which implies your data stays in your own storage. A community comment notes that data is transformed into Parquet/Delta, though the platform's scale optimizations are proprietary. OpenSharing lets you share data with non-Databricks users, but that is sharing, not a documented bulk export or exit path. missing for 10: a documented export-all or offboarding capability, first-party statement that Delta/Parquet storage is open and readable outside Databricks, coverage of non-table assets (notebooks, dashboards, models), and independent hands-on corroboration of a migration out.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: It runs directly on your data lake, supports ANSI SQL with Delta Lake extensions, and provides the tools to build highly performant, cost-effective data warehouses without moving your data.
Users are steered toward its tech to transform data into Parquet/Delta
lets you share data and AI assets with users outside your organization, regardless of whether they use Databricks
